tasks.short: Keep avionics maintenance and repair records.

steps.what: Capture and verify actual maintenance and repair evidence for the aircraft and component
Write records of maintenance and repair work in the aviation maintenance system {OTHER}

loop.purpose: Draft a maintenance record from actual captured work evidence
loop.input: Actual aircraft/component identity, fault, action, parts, hours and test evidence
loop.check: Technician checks actual work meaning, omitted defects, incorrect completion claims and part or test references against actual work evidence
loop.stop: Missing actual evidence or one failed correction returns writing to manual entry
loop.why_not_simpler: Native aircraft and work-order fields come first; varied fault and action descriptions need bounded prose

steps.what: Check the complete final maintenance record and exact aircraft/component destination
Commit the checked final avionics maintenance record

tasks.design: Use native aircraft, component and work-order fields in the aviation maintenance system {OTHER}, then add a bounded draft for actual fault and action descriptions. The technician captures real work evidence and checks the exact final record before committing; no draft issues a release to service.
tasks.previous_blocker: Maintenance records can repeat identifiers and require narrative writing from actual work evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Native digital maintenance records and bounded prose drafting can reduce repeated entry while retaining record checks.
tasks.still_hard: A complete-looking record may omit a defect or wrongly imply a test or repair was completed.
tasks.human_edge: The technician knows what work actually occurred and what remains unresolved.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft record writing; maintenance and certification rights stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: AMOS Production supports digital work-order completion, aircraft-side recording and integrated e-signature; this supports the record workflow, not the proposed language drafting or a local saving.
Model knowledge: bounded source-linked drafting can assist fault and action descriptions but requires technician verification.

assumptions: Boundary is keeping actual maintenance and repair records, not performing the repair or signing release to service. Actual certification remains a separate authorised staff action with no saved certification labour claimed.

Technician captures actual aircraft registration, component serial, work-order identifier, fault, action, part, hours and actual test reference in s1. Actual source capture is fully counted there; missing evidence is obtained manually and never generated. s2 drafts only from verified evidence.
Test native maintenance forms and field reuse before code. Existing digital capture earns no new saving. Draft correction remains in s2 and the actual final record check remains in s3.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system commit is one percent fully retained; the check is existing record work, not an added approval ceremony.
unknowns: What record writing is still repeated?
Does the aviation maintenance system permit appropriately controlled drafting?
research_questions: Does assisted drafting reduce record effort after capture, omissions correction and complete final checking?

already_counted.description: Correct generated maintenance narrative within s2.

incremental.description: Maintain record mappings and audit incorrect completion implications after updates.

approvals.approved_version: s3 checked final avionics maintenance record, exact aircraft/component and work-order destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 45*0.40 narrative = 18; subtract 1.5 upkeep = 16.5. If only half the narrative can be assisted, 9 minus 1.5 = 7.5. Actual capture, final checks and commit remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test and troubleshoot avionics components and assemblies.

steps.what: Find and assess actual circuit diagrams, fault history and test procedures
Test and troubleshoot instruments, components and assemblies with actual electrical test instruments
outputs: actual electrical test observations and readings

steps.what: Diagnose the actual avionics fault and decide further test or repair needs
inputs: actual electrical test observations and readings

steps.what: Write and check actual test readings and troubleshooting findings
inputs: actual electrical test observations and readings

steps.what: Save the checked actual avionics troubleshooting record

tasks.design: Configure component and revision filters in {DOCS} and the aviation maintenance system {OTHER}. The technician reads the procedure, performs actual tests, diagnoses the fault and writes and checks actual readings; only finding the applicable document changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correct test documents can be scattered across component and aircraft revisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native identifier and applicability filters can shorten document finding.
tasks.still_hard: Probe placement, intermittent faults and safe test interpretation require hands-on skill.
tasks.human_edge: The technician notices a physical condition that the fault description does not capture.
tasks.altitude: Less document finding; troubleshooting responsibility stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: controlled maintenance document filters can reduce retrieval by component and revision; they do not perform or interpret electrical tests.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual testing, troubleshooting and its existing findings record. Routine full maintenance-record composition is a different task; team roll-ups must resolve actual record ownership rather than add duplicate record effort.

Document owners supply actual aircraft/component identifier, applicability and revision; technician verifies them in s1. All actual readings and observations are produced and captured by the technician in s2-s4. Missing metadata and unsupported sources remain manual.

Test native filters before code. Existing filtered lookup earns no saving. Fixed record fields and native instrument exports are tested, but unsupported instrument connections and variable fault descriptions provide no justified record-time cut in this scenario.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Same-system save retains its one percent share; the existing findings check supplies its gate.
unknowns: Are test procedures already filtered by applicability?
Do actual test instruments support compatible exports?
research_questions: Does native filtering reduce finding while preserving procedure reading and correct applicability checks?

incremental.description: Maintain component and revision retrieval filters.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final actual avionics troubleshooting record and exact aircraft/component destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10*0.30 document finding = 3; minus 0.5 upkeep = 2.5. If half the documents can be retrieved through reliable metadata, 1.5 minus 0.5 = 1. Hands-on tests, diagnosis and actual record work stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate with aircraft engineers and maintenance personnel.

steps.what: Find actual aircraft work status, dependencies and engineering restrictions
Coordinate work with engineers, technicians and other aircraft maintenance personnel
Enter and check actual agreed work dependencies and handover notes
Commit the checked actual aircraft coordination update

tasks.design: Configure a native aircraft-work view in the aviation maintenance system {OTHER} and linked work-item fields in {PROJECT}. The technician still coordinates with colleagues and writes actual agreements; only status finding and repeated work-order references change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination can require finding work status and repeating work-order references in handover updates.
tasks.enabler_now: Native work views and linked dependency fields can reuse actual current records.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, access restrictions and safe sequencing need actual staff agreement.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises dependencies that current work status does not express and negotiates a workable sequence.
tasks.altitude: Less status lookup; maintenance coordination authority stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native work-order views and linked dependency fields can reduce status finding and repeated references; they do not negotiate maintenance sequencing.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual coordination and existing handover/dependency entries. Do not add a handover report to an oral-only exchange; reweight to actual work. Other personnel's time is outside this denominator.

Work-order owners supply actual identifier, aircraft, status, restriction and timestamp. The technician checks context in s1 and captures actual agreements in s3 after s2. Missing or stale status is resolved manually; a dashboard does not invent completion or colleague agreement.
Test native views and linked fields before code. Existing views earn no new saving. Only repeated status finding and identifier entry change, not agreement capture or coordination judgement.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Final commit is one percent fully retained and uses the existing update check.
unknowns: Are work orders already visible in one current view?
Which coordination entries are actually written?
research_questions: Can native views reduce lookup without treating stale status as an actual agreement?

incremental.description: Maintain coordination filters and work-item links.

approvals.approved_version: s3 checked final aircraft coordination update and exact work-item destinations; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10*0.40 lookup + 14*0.20 repeated references = 6.8; subtract 0.5 upkeep = 6.3. With half those lookups and fields eligible, 3.4 minus 0.5 = 2.9. Actual coordination and commit time remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Interpret flight-test data to diagnose avionics problems.

steps.what: Collect and verify actual flight test data and event references
Prepare time-aligned flight-test plots from verified channels and events
Interpret flight test data to diagnose malfunctions and systemic performance problems
Write and check actual flight-test diagnostic findings and supporting evidence

loop.purpose: Draft the diagnostic record from the technician's actual interpretation
loop.input: Actual chosen diagnosis, limitations and verified source plots
loop.check: Technician checks causal meaning, omitted events, unsupported fault claims and consistency with actual interpretation
loop.stop: Missing diagnosis or two failed drafts returns writing to the technician
loop.why_not_simpler: Native plots and fixed record fields come first; diagnostic explanations vary with actual findings

steps.what: Save the checked actual flight-test diagnostic record

tasks.design: Test native flight-test imports and time-aligned plot configurations in the test analysis system {OTHER}. The technician verifies channel mapping and event alignment, interprets malfunctions and checks a bounded draft of the actual diagnostic narrative before saving it; no model diagnoses or clears an aircraft.
tasks.previous_blocker: Flight-test review can repeat channel imports, time alignment, plot preparation and narrative writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native import and plot configuration can reuse actual test channels; bounded drafting can start from the technician's actual diagnosis.
tasks.still_hard: Configuration changes, sensor faults and coupled system behaviour require specialist diagnosis.
tasks.human_edge: The technician distinguishes a real malfunction from a test or sensor artefact.
tasks.altitude: Less data preparation; diagnostic and aircraft release rights remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: test-analysis tools can import channels and reuse plots; bounded language drafting can support technician-chosen findings but cannot establish an avionics diagnosis.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual flight-data interpretation and existing diagnostic record. Test-flight conduct, repairs and release to service belong to actual owners and have no avoided labour claimed.

Flight-test system supplies actual aircraft/configuration identifier, channel, timestamp, value, unit and event markers. The technician verifies channel units, time origin and gaps in s1; missing mappings and uncertain alignment stay manual before s2. Diagnosis is created by the technician in s3 before s4 drafts it.

Test native imports and plotting before code. Already-automated plots and test-system runtime earn no labour saving. Diagnostic judgement stays fully retained and all generated-meaning correction remains in s4.
Shares and reductions are provisional, not measured baselines. Same-system save is one percent fully retained and uses the existing diagnostic-record check.
unknowns: Are flight-test channels and plots already linked automatically?
How much actual diagnostic writing is repeated?
research_questions: Can native plots reproduce actual event alignment without hiding dropped channels or configuration changes?

already_counted.description: Correct diagnostic narrative meaning within s4.

incremental.description: Maintain channel mappings, plotting definitions and diagnostic drafting checks.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final flight-test diagnostic record and exact aircraft/test document destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.50 data entry + 15 plot work + 14*0.30 prose = 29.2; subtract 2 upkeep = 27.2. If half the preparation and prose are eligible, 14.6 minus 2 = 12.6. Diagnosis and final save retain all time.

role.altitude: Hands-on testing, diagnosis and actual certification authority stay unchanged while repeated avionics information handling can shrink.
